solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enterprise maybe with sailors in their natural environment

indicators.note: the sailors are placed in the middle of their own environment, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a ship is where sailors naturally belong
tars is an old word for sailors

explanation.surface: A navy vessel's crew looks perfectly at home aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Enterprise is the spaceship in Star Trek, hence the 'maybe' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enterprise of Star Trek is an example of a spacefaring vessel, so it stands for one.

clue.text: End of skirt raised to reveal it?

definitions.text: End of skirt raised to reveal it?

indicators.note: the end of the word skirt is its final letter

parts.note: raised means high, lifted up

explanation.surface: A hemline lifted to show off a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: lift the skirt's end and this body part shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitching a hem up exposes the upper leg, the part of the body revealed.

clue.text: Wild tiger, menace where there are lots of horses

definitions.text: where there are lots of horses

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A savage big cat threatens a place full of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of horse racing at a course gathers many runners, so horses abound there.

clue.text: Man had new identity as female servant

indicators.note: new says the letters of man had are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ID is the standard abbreviation for identity

explanation.surface: A man took on a new persona, posing as a maid.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical and old-fashioned term for a woman who waits on a mistress, a maidservant.

clue.text: Proverbial thief running in a strip cartoon

indicators.note: running suggests the letters moving about freely into another order

explanation.surface: A robber dashing through the panels of a comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Procrastination is the thief of time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known saying calls delaying things the thief of time, so the habit is a proverbial robber.

clue.text: Sweet child, writer of verse keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a poet writes verse
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A lovely child, and a poet who keeps hushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term of endearment for a small, sweet person, a darling.

clue.text: Seller of fruit securing heartless deal

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the fruit wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: heartless strips out the middle of deal, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A fruit trader seals a poor bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling hawker who sells small goods from door to door is a seller.

clue.text: A salesperson turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative; the letters also sitting inside salesperson is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A sales rep arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is the definition, as in '£5 a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: In prices such as 'ten pounds a day' the article means for each, the Latin-derived word.

clue.text: No longer facing stress, additional time being granted

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
tension is stress

explanation.surface: Freed from pressure now that a deadline has been extended.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadlines or loans get prolonged by a grant of more time, the term for that allowance.

clue.text: Sealed container of ancient civilisation found after short time

indicators.note: found after places the civilisation piece behind the time piece

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Incan describes the ancient civilisation of the Incas in Peru

explanation.surface: An archaeologist dates a sealed jar of a lost civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal can, sealed to keep food, is a common container.

clue.text: Pig-headed old boy taking time to admit "game over"

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the time takes the other piece inside

parts.note: a date is a time

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for the game is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: A stubborn former pupil takes a while before conceding the match is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn and unyielding, refusing to change one's mind, as pig-headed implies.

clue.text: Son (Noah's son) is phoney

parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's three sons in Genesis

explanation.surface: A boy, son of Noah, turns out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fake or pretended is a synonym of phoney.

clue.text: Holy mother engaging philosopher about Roman politician

indicators.note: engaging means taking on, holding the others inside

parts.note: Mary is the mother of Jesus
Immanuel Kant, the German philosopher
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: The Virgin Mary takes on a thinker over a Roman statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The ally of Julius Caesar and lover of Cleopatra was a leading statesman of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Most stare at silly person raising a glass

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behaving foolishly, jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: Most people gape at a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal dinner the official who proposes toasts lifts a drink to lead them.

clue.text: Restaurants serving terrible teas across lake

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the shuffled teas spread around the lake
terrible suggests the teas are mangled into a different order

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Cafes beside a lake serving awful tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the teas into EATS, which 'across' then wraps round the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for places where people dine, such as cafes and diners.

clue.text: Old instrument, a sort able to move around

indicators.note: to move around says the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An antique device of a type that can be carried about.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval navigational device for measuring star altitudes is an old instrument.

clue.text: Keen biblical king abandoning his capital

indicators.note: his capital here is the king's capital letter, his initial, which is dropped

parts.note: David was king of Israel in the Bible

explanation.surface: An eager king of Israel leaves Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city, Jerusalem; it is the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and enthusiastic, as a keen fan is, is a plain synonym.

clue.text: University place — Rod mostly seen therein as a hit

indicators.note: seen therein says the rod piece is found inside the place piece

parts.note: to put is to place

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a rod

explanation.surface: A college spot where a fishing rod becomes a success.
explanation.walkthrough: A perch, or rod, is an old British unit of length of about five metres; 'mostly' trims its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing punch thrown upward to the chin is a kind of hit.

clue.text: Small case in one American truck heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a ute is a utility vehicle, a pickup truck

explanation.surface: A little box inside a pickup driving west.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics is the crossword-familiar term.

clue.text: Trouble-maker, having taken old red wine, unable to act

parts.note: an imp is a mischief-maker
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who has drunk aged claret is left powerless.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerless or helpless, without the ability to do anything.

clue.text: Do a bunk in vehicle during period of tenancy

indicators.note: during means in the midst of, so the vehicle sits inside the tenancy

parts.note: a let is a period of renting a property
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Escaping in a van halfway through a lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do a bunk' is British slang for run away, especially from debts.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for absconding without paying debts, the same sense as doing a runner.

clue.text: Get together in new gang? Coterie I'll have no part in

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
the letter is excluded from the mix, having no share in it

parts.note: I'll begins with I, the one letter excluded

explanation.surface: A newly formed gang meets; a clique member refuses to join.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle GANG and COTERIE together without the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather or assemble in a crowd is to meet up together.

clue.text: Pulpit used by William Booth

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army's founder preaching from his stand.
explanation.walkthrough: William Booth founded the Salvation Army, a Christian preaching movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An early Christian raised reading desk, a lectern serving as pulpit.

clue.text: Half-hearted shout in the basement?

indicators.note: the heart of the shout is a doubled letter, and half of that is lost

parts.note: a bellow is a loud shout

explanation.surface: A feeble cry from the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLOW has LL at its heart; losing half leaves one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstairs, under the ground floor, is where a cellar lies.

clue.text: Beef in doughy food mostly had by foreign friend

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: pastry is food made of dough
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: Meat inside a pie, largely shared with a French pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned, smoked cured beef is a type of the meat.

clue.text: Quaint little wife coming out to give support

indicators.note: coming out means leaving, so the wife's letter is removed

parts.note: twee means quaint, overly cute
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A twee little wife steps forward to back someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfer's peg that holds the ball up is a support.

clue.text: Sea creature to sink, head disappearing

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter, which vanishes

parts.note: to scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately

explanation.surface: A sea animal sinking, its head vanishing below the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish, a squid-like mollusc, is a marine animal.

clue.text: Stick carried by policemen — truncheon

indicators.note: carried by says the letters are held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A baton carried by officers: the truncheon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like the truncheon itself; it is the verb, to glue.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind or glue things together, as mortar or adhesive does.

clue.text: Brunette in group of teachers meeting ex-PM

parts.note: NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister 2007-10

explanation.surface: A dark-haired member of a teachers' union meeting a former Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazel-coloured hair shade describes a dark-haired person.
